tip: 'Man' is the impersonal 'one', people in general: 'man ska vara försiktig' = one should be careful.
'Tillbaka' attaches to the verb like English 'back': 'ringa tillbaka' = call back.
'Brukar' marks a habit, something usually done: 'det brukar ta' = it usually takes.
Double definite with an en-word: 'den' + 'svarta' + 'katten'. The adjective normally ends in -a in the definite form.
When 'what' is the subject of an indirect question, add 'som': 'vad som hände' = what happened.
En-words ending in -a normally form the definite plural with -orna: 'blomma' becomes 'blommorna', the flowers.
'Till' pairs a side with a dish, meaning to go with: 'potatismos till köttbullarna'.
To show possession, Swedish adds just -s, no apostrophe: 'husets specialitet' = the house's specialty.
'Sommar' has an irregular plural: 'en sommar' but 'somrar', so 'somrarna' = the summers.
'Hår' is an ett-word: 'det röda håret' shows the double definite with an adjective.
'Var' is the command form of 'vara' (to be): 'var försiktig' = be careful.
'Med' can mean 'by means of': 'med posten' = by mail.
'Skit samma' is a crude, slangy way to say 'whatever'. Keep it for casual speech only.
'Ihop' means together and attaches to the verb: 'samlade ihop pengar' = collected money.
'Passa sig' means watch out, and the pronoun matches the person: 'passa dig'.
You can stack 'sin' with a possessive -s: 'sin dotters födelsedag' = her own daughter's birthday.
After 'börja', 'att' before the next verb is optional: 'började jobba' = started working.
After the verb, 'om' can mean 're-' or 'again': 'målade om' = repainted.
'Lyssna på' = listen to; the 'på' is required: 'jag lyssnade på henne'.
'Vilken'/'vilket' plus a noun makes an exclamation: 'vilken otur' = what bad luck.
'Vore' is the 'would be' form of 'vara', for hypotheticals: 'det vore trevligt' = it would be nice.
'Hinna med' = manage to catch in time: 'hann inte med den' = didn't make it.
'Det var länge sedan' = it's been a long time since: 'länge sedan jag pratade svenska'.
Front the adjective for emphasis, then 'som': 'duktig som hon är' = skilled as she is.
Swedish commands drop the subject: 'stäng' is the bare verb, no 'du'. 'Stäng fönstret' = close the window.
'Det gör inget' is a set phrase for 'it doesn't matter', literally 'it does nothing'.
As an adverb here, 'lugn' takes the neuter -t: 'lugnt'. 'Ta det lugnt' is the fixed phrase for 'take it easy'.
En-words ending in -a normally form the definite plural with -orna: 'räka' becomes 'räkorna' (the shrimp).
'Rasta' specifically means to walk or exercise an animal: 'han rastar hunden' (he walks the dog).
'Framme' means already there or up ahead at a spot; 'fram' is for motion toward: 'övergångsstället är framme'.
